To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) context dependency of mutations in grass chloroplasts is correlated with the local base composition and the number of flank pyrimidines, and (2) the context-dependent mutation dynamics of grass chloroplast DNA are sufficient to generate both compositional differences between silent sites of coding and noncoding DNA as well as codon usage bias in low-expression chloroplast DNA.

the mutation dynamics of chloroplast DNA (including both base substitution rates and indels) are strongly influenced by the flanking base context and that these dynamics can account for the observed compositional differences between coding and noncoding sites as well as for the codon usage bias of low-expression chloroplastic genes.

context-dependent mutations in chloroplast genomes can account for much of the observed base compositional bias and can generate codon bias in a manner consistent with weak selection for optimal translation efficiency.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the evolution of the chloroplast genome in grasses and, specifically, with the influence of local sequence context on mutation and selection.
the influence of local base sequence composition on the dynamics of mutations in chloroplast genomes.
the role of selection and mutation in generating the composition bias of chloroplast DNA.
